title: Create a round-trip screen proposal workflow
summary: This vertical slice is the proof that HumbleStudio can complement Figma: edits remain attached to real components, tokens, navigation, source paths, tickets, and repository revisions rather than becoming isolated mockups.
acceptance_criteria: The session pins repository, source revision, view ID, snapshot, component definitions, navigation evidence, and owning ticket before edits begin.

Supported edits include at least component instance placement/variant, spacing/layout constraints, token substitution, localized text proposal, and navigation annotation; unsupported edits remain visibly non-applicable.
Validation detects stale source revision, missing component/token, accessibility/localization risk, constraint conflicts, and changes outside the selected screen scope.
The handoff artifact contains before/after Board state, screenshots, structured commands/deltas, source targets, acceptance criteria, unresolved decisions, and repository-qualified ticket references.
Re-importing a newer bundle performs a three-way reconciliation between old source, proposal overrides, and new source and never discards user work silently.
The first reference fixture uses a real repository export and proves import, edit, proposal, simulated implementation refresh, and resolved/diverged status end to end.
The complete user journey is demonstrated from entry to a useful, recoverable result, including empty, loading, stale/offline, failure, and retry states.

The experience uses the repository's localization source of truth, supports Dynamic Type or platform text scaling, exposes meaningful accessibility labels/actions, and respects reduced-motion preferences where motion is present.
User-visible claims and recommendations remain explainable and conservative; the UI distinguishes observed data, inferred guidance, planned work, and unavailable evidence.
Focused behavior tests and a repeatable visual or runtime evidence artifact protect the primary journey without relying only on implementation snapshots.
The strongest practical repository-native build, test, lint, contract, and diff gates pass with zero app-owned warnings; warnings are not hidden by suppression or threshold changes.

evidence.note: The existing product contract requires proposal-first, auditable authoring.
Board edits already generate reviewed proposals rather than direct source mutation.
Revision-aware repository artifacts protect round-trip identity.
Reusable components and constraints enable meaningful structured screen edits.

agent_notes: Portfolio Evolution Wave 2; experience north-star ticket.
Estimated effort: XL, 6-10 focused working days

User outcome: Jan can visually improve a real app screen, hand Codex an exact reviewable change plan, and later see whether the repository implementation matches, diverges, or supersedes the proposal.
Non-scope: Do not apply changes automatically to source code, claim pixel-perfect reconstruction of arbitrary screenshots, or support every component property in the first vertical slice.

Alternative considered and rejected: Export a static annotated screenshot and prose task — that loses structured component identity, validation, three-way reconciliation, and machine-readable implementation targets.
Do not broaden the slice into unrelated cleanup, framework migration, release publication, or source-of-truth changes outside the ticket.
Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain; priority band next. The technical north star and signature journey remain useful after the professional baseline is established.
Wave 10 final rationalization: merge-into-product-roadmap; portfolio band next. North-star and flagship work is consolidated into the repository charter and capstone journey.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `supporting-input`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-supporting`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `use as product context, not as a parallel implementation stream`. Product north-star and flagship intent remain useful, but implementation is now owned by Wave 11 and completion work.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-product-evidence` / `next` / priority `medium`. Product north-star and flagship journey remain useful research and design inputs.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Product north-star and flagship journey remain useful research and design inputs.
